metric.semantic_determinacy.limitations: This is a single-language (C++-only) shard. The frozen basis for cross-language ranking (spec's 'common basis' of probes where all 10 languages have a fragment) cannot be computed from this shard alone; the runner must merge this raw per-probe B_i table with the other language shards before any comparability gate or common-basis recomputation is applied. The reported normalized score (90.02) uses a frozen, language-neutral CAP=3.0 reference scale applied identically to every language shard so it is directly comparable without waiting for the merge, but the authoritative common-basis figure is runner-computed.
metric.semantic_determinacy.methodology_basis: spec 6.1.3.B (semantic_compression.md). Raw value = mean(log2(B_i)) over the 44 frozen probes, B_i = count of materially different interpretations compatible with the probe's LOCAL surface form alone (before consulting external declarations/signatures except where the probe explicitly includes the callee declaration inside measured_fragment, e.g. F05.P2/F06.P1/F06.P2). Lower mean(log2(B_i)) is better (spec: 'Lower semantic branching is better').
metric.semantic_determinacy.normalization_rule: score = 100 * clamp(1 - mean_log2B / CAP, 0, 1), with CAP = 3.0 (a fixed, pre-declared reference ceiling equal to mean(log2(B_i)) if every probe averaged B=8 branching outcomes; this ceiling is frozen and applied identically regardless of language so it does not bias any language). mean_log2B_for_C++ = 0.29931818..., score = 100*(1 - 0.29931818/3) = 90.0227 -> rounded 90.02.

F01.P1.reason: `const int n = 7; return n;` — const local scalar is unambiguous: fixed value, fixed storage, non-reassignable, initialized. No plausible alternative reading of this exact surface form.

F01.P2.reason: `static int64_t counter = 0;` at namespace scope plus `constexpr int64_t LIMIT = 100;` — internal linkage for the mutable var is explicit via `static`, but a reader of the bare pair could also plausibly read `counter` as having external linkage if `static` were dropped by a less careful author, and constexpr-vs-const semantics for LIMIT (compile-time constant vs merely read-only) are two live readings the bare tokens leave open until the exact keyword is parsed.

F02.P1.reason: `int v;` alone (before the branch is seen) is compatible both with 'genuinely indeterminate value, UB if read early' and 'definitely-assigned-before-use enforced by the following control flow' — C++ has no compiler-checked definite-assignment analysis, so the local form does not itself disambiguate until the whole branch is read.

F02.P2.reason: `std::array<uint8_t,16> buf;` (or `unsigned char buf[16];`) with no initializer is unambiguously indeterminate content in C++; well-established single reading.

F03.P1.reason: `x++;` (or `x += 1;`) on `int32_t` — C++ signed overflow is undefined behavior (no checked mode exists for C++ per toolchain_binding.safety_mode_clause), so the local form is compatible with both 'wraps like two's complement' and 'traps/UB, arbitrary observable behavior', which are materially different outcomes.

F03.P2.reason: `xs[1] = 42;` on `std::vector<int>` — in-place element write through the existing binding is the single ordinary reading; operator[] is well known to write through, not rebind.

F04.P1.reason: `int& port = slot; port = 9;` — C++ reference binding is a single, fully explicit writable alias with no other standard reading.

F04.P2.reason: `std::span<const int> window(xs);` — non-owning, read-only, non-copying view is the one standard reading of `std::span<const T>`.

F04.P3.reason: Identity compared via raw pointer/`shared_ptr::get()` equality is unambiguous pointer/address identity, distinct from value equality by construction of the chosen operation.

F05.P1.reason: Bare call `f(x)` with `f`'s declaration excluded from the fragment (per probe design) is maximally ambiguous in C++: the call syntax is IDENTICAL whether `f` takes `std::vector<int>` by value (copy, no caller-visible mutation), `std::vector<int>&` (full read/write alias, callee may replace/resize), `const std::vector<int>&` (read-only alias), `std::vector<int>*` /pointer, or retains the reference beyond the call via a stored member. All ~6 outcomes enumerated in the probe's SCORING NOTE remain live for C++'s call-site syntax alone, which is the language fact the glyph-neutrality rule (spec 6.1.4.B) is designed to surface.

F05.P2.reason: Probe includes `put`'s full signature `void put(int& cell)` inside the measured fragment; `int&` parameter is unambiguous writable alias, single reading.

F05.P3.reason: `auto neg = [k](int a){ return k - a; };` — explicit capture list `[k]` and lambda syntax leave one standard reading (capture by value, closure object).

F06.P1.reason: `int mid(std::vector<int> v){ return v[1]; }` — return type `int` (by value) is an unambiguous independent copy; no aliasing with the caller's vector is possible for a plain `int`.

F06.P2.reason: `std::tuple<int,int> divmod2(...)` with `auto [q,r] = divmod2(a,b);` structured bindings — single explicit reading of two independent int results.

F07.P1.reason: `int r = a*b + c;` with all operand types already fixed as `int32_t` in given context — ordinary precedence and type are the single standard reading (overflow behavior itself is covered by metric D/hidden-cost, not branching of THIS site's arithmetic shape).

F07.P2.reason: `int q = a/b; int m = a%b;` — C++ (>=C++11) mandates truncation-toward-zero division and a remainder whose sign matches the dividend, but this is a language-specification fact not visible in the bare `/` and `%` tokens; a reader relying on the surface form alone could equally expect floor-division semantics (as in Python) or truncation, which are materially different results for negative operands.

F08.P1.reason: `int32_t o = m + 1;` at `m == INT32_MAX`, using the plain operator (rung iv, since C++ offers no standard checked/wrapping/saturating integer op) — signed overflow is undefined behavior in C++, so the surface form is compatible with wrap, trap/crash, silently-produce-any-value, or the compiler assuming the overflow cannot happen and eliminating a subsequent check (a documented real optimizer behavior) — four materially different outcomes.

F08.P2.reason: Explicit `if (b == 0) { q = 0; } else { q = a / b; }` guard makes the zero-divisor outcome fully determinate at the site; single reading.

F09.P1.reason: `bool eq = (s1 == s2);` on `std::string` — operator== for std::string is specified value/content equality, not identity; single standard reading.

F09.P2.reason: `std::sort(xs.rbegin(), xs.rend());` with `bool lt = a < b;` — in-place reordering via reverse iterators is a single, well-known reading (std::sort mutates its iterator range in place, no new sequence).

F10.P1.reason: `int32_t small = static_cast<int32_t>(big);` — explicit narrowing cast is visible, but the OUT-OF-RANGE outcome (modulo-2^n wrap, defined since C++20, versus the pre-C++20 implementation-defined status many readers still assume) is not disambiguated by the cast token alone; two materially different expectations persist without consulting the exact standard version.

F10.P2.reason: `double sum = i + d;` — implicit usual-arithmetic-conversion of `int` to `double` is invisible at the operator; a reader could equally (incorrectly) expect `d` to convert toward int, or expect a compiler warning/error, so two live readings of 'which operand converts' persist from the bare `+` alone.

F11.P1.reason: `int e = xs[i];` using vector operator[] (R10's fewest-token ordinary form) performs NO bounds check; out-of-range `i` is undefined behavior. The surface form is compatible with (a) silent garbage/misread value, (b) crash/segfault, or (c) apparently-correct-but-wrong value due to UB-based optimization — three materially different outcomes remain open at the plain `[]` site.

F11.P2.reason: `std::span<int> part(xs.data()+1, 3);` — std::span's declared type is an explicit non-owning view; single reading that no copy occurs and writes-through-alias are possible.

F12.P1.reason: `std::optional<int> o = std::nullopt; int n = o.value_or(0);` — fully explicit standard optional API; single reading.

F12.P2.reason: Substituted explicit `if (o.has_value()) { p = h(*o); } else { p = std::nullopt; }` (C++20 lacks std::optional::transform/and_then, added only in C++23) is fully determinate despite being a P-a substitution; explicit control flow leaves one reading.

F13.P1.reason: `int parse_twice(std::string s){ return 2*std::stoi(s); }` — the function's DECLARED interface (`int parse_twice(std::string)`) gives no visible indication that the function can fail; C++ has no checked-exceptions annotation. A reader of the signature alone could reasonably believe the function never fails, or (correctly) know std::stoi throws — two materially different beliefs about failure visibility survive from the local declaration alone.

F13.P2.reason: Explicit `try { n = std::stoi(s); } catch (...) { n = 0; }` makes the protected region and the fallback fully determinate; single reading.

F14.P1.reason: `std::variant<Circle, Rect> s = Circle{2.0};` — variant's fixed template argument list is a single, explicitly closed alternative set.

F14.P2.reason: `double area = std::visit(overloaded{ [](const Circle& c){...}, [](const Rect& r){...} }, s);` — the overloaded-lambda visitor pattern requires the visitor to be callable with every alternative or the program fails to compile, giving a single reading that all cases are handled.

F14.P3.reason: Abstract base `struct Shape { virtual double area() const = 0; };` with `Tri : Shape` defined in a separate translation unit and dispatched through a `Shape&`/pointer — ordinary, single-reading virtual dispatch.

F15.P1.reason: `template<typename T> T head(std::vector<T> xs){ return xs[0]; }` — template instantiation for each call type is a single, statically-checked reading with no erasure ambiguity.

F15.P2.reason: `template<typename T> requires std::totally_ordered<T> T max_of(T a, T b){ return a>b?a:b; }` — C++20 concept constraint at the declaration is a single explicit reading, diagnosed at the template definition/instantiation boundary the concept defines.

F15.P3.reason: Abstract `struct Named { virtual std::string tag() const = 0; };` with `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Named>> items` holding `A` and `B` instances, dispatched via `items[0]->tag()` — single, ordinary virtual-dispatch reading.

F16.P1.reason: `int total = std::accumulate(xs.begin(), xs.end(), 0);` — single standard reading of a left-to-right sum.

F16.P2.reason: `for (auto& [k,v] : mp) total += v;` plus `auto it = mp.find("b"); int miss = (it==mp.end())?0:it->second;` — explicit find/end check makes the miss outcome fully determinate at the site; unordered_map's unspecified iteration order does not change the SUM's observable result, so it is not a materially different outcome for this site.

F17.P1.reason: `std::ifstream in("data.txt");` as a local RAII object — C++ guarantees the destructor runs deterministically at scope exit on every path including exceptions; single reading.

F17.P2.reason: User-defined destructor `~Handle(){ ++released; }` invoked deterministically and exactly once at end of block scope; single, canonical C++ RAII reading.

F18.P1.reason: `#include <iostream>` plus `std::cout << "x\n";` — single ordinary reading of which names enter scope and from where.

F18.P2.reason: `secret()` defined `static`/in an anonymous namespace in util.cpp (internal linkage), `pub_add` given external linkage and declared in a header used from FILE.cpp — single, classical C++ translation-unit encapsulation reading.

F19.P1.reason: `auto fa = std::async(std::launch::async, [](){return 20;}); auto fb = std::async(std::launch::async, [](){return 22;}); int sum = fa.get()+fb.get();` — explicit `std::launch::async` policy removes the implementation-defined async-vs-deferred ambiguity, leaving a single reading.

F19.P2.reason: `std::atomic<int64_t> counter{0};` with `counter.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed)` from two threads — std::atomic's normative guarantee of atomic read-modify-write is a single, documented reading.

F20.P1.reason: `extern "C" int abs(int);` then `int r = abs(-3);` — explicit extern "C" declaration is a single, unambiguous FFI reading.

F20.P2.reason: `extern "C" int add2(int a, int b){ return a+b; }` — explicit extern "C" export with C ABI and unmangled symbol is a single reading.
